summary: r2 APPROVE. All four r1 blocking fixes are genuinely applied in the spec BODY (not merely claimed in the §10 changelog), each is correct, and the revision introduces NO new correctness holes. I re-verified every fix against the spec text and spot-checked the corrected template pointer against the actual source. The design core (canonical Q6_K/Q5_K_M layouts §3, the pure-source signed technique §4.1/§7, the zero-compiler-change claim, Q6_K-first phasing §2, the Q6_K non-fusion decision §4.3) is unchanged from r1 and remains byte-for-byte correct against ggml k_quants. One NON-BLOCKING observation on AT-2823 (now near-redundant with AT-2822) is noted below; it does not gate coding.
fix_verification: FIX 1 (AT-2811 full-256 golden) — APPLIED & COMPLETE. AT-2811 (line 293) now mandates the golden be the FULL 256-element decoded f32 array (every weight verified) and enumerates the required coverage: (i) all four quant-groups q1/q2/q3/q4 = the two ql slices x lo/hi nibble x qh bit-pairs 0-1/2-3/4-5/6-7; (ii) BOTH 128-halves h=0/h=1 (the 64h/32h/128h/8h advances); (iii) the is=l/16 boundary (l=15 vs l=16, selecting adjacent sc entries); (iv) >=1 negative int8 scale; (v) q extremes q=0->-32 / q=63->+31. Because the golden is the full 256-element decode, the 4-groups x 2-halves x is-boundary product is covered BY CONSTRUCTION (every element is one of q1..q4 in one of the two halves); the enumerated (iv)/(v) are data-construction requirements on the fixture and are stated. No gap — a group-3/half-1/is-boundary decode bug cannot pass.

FIX 2 (AT-2823 re-gate to f32accum oracle) — APPLIED & CORRECT. AT-2823 (line 309) now compares the coopmat Q5 kernel against the q5k_dequant_matmul_f32accum_cpu oracle (which rounds weights f32->f16->f32, apples-to-apples with the coopmat f32_to_f16 A-staging), combined <= 1e-3, and explicitly REMOVES the false 'mirror AT-1803 bit-identity' framing (it now states the portable-vs-coopmat comparison is a cross-PRECISION ~5e-4 gap, not ~1e-6 bit-identity). The oracle does NOT dangle: q5k_dequant_matmul_f32accum_cpu is a §5.2 deliverable, its dequant core is golden-verified by AT-2816 and metric-sanity-checked by AT-2817, and it structurally mirrors the trusted q4km_oracle f32accum reference. The 'f16-weight-rounded' rounding is precisely pinned: §5 line 255 mandates REUSE of q4km_oracle::round_f32_to_f16_to_f32 (single source of truth, the same RTNE function already validated for the Q4_K_M coopmat AT-1800..1802 path that the coopmat kernel's f32_to_f16 matches). Coder has an unambiguous match target.

FIX 3 (builtin-set ⊆ baseline) — APPLIED to all three anchors. AT-2813 (line 295), AT-2818 (line 304), AT-2821 (line 307) are reworded from the literally-false 'references only reserved Q4_0 builtins' to 'referenced-builtin set is a SUBSET of the corresponding Q4_K_M baseline kernel's builtin set — no addition', each with the explicit note that band/bor/shl/lshr/gid/f32_from_u32/f16_bits_to_f32/coopmat_* are legitimately NOT in RESERVED_Q4_0_BUILTIN_NAMES and the meaningful check is set-⊆-baseline. AT-2821 also spells out shared_memory_bytes==4096 = (512+512)*2 f16 + (256+256)*4 f32 (arithmetically correct). Mechanically implementable via the existing capability_extension_sets() helper.

FIX 4 (bit-exact template pointer + associativity) — APPLIED & VERIFIED IN-SOURCE. §5 (lines 220-232, 247-249) now points the Coder at crates/axc-driver/tests/common_matmul.rs::q4km_dequant_matmul_cpu as the bit-exact template (was incorrectly 'mirror q4km_oracle.rs'), while still reusing the metric fns from q4km_oracle. I confirmed the target fn EXISTS at common_matmul.rs:118 and that it groups as (d*sc)*nib - (dmin*m) (d1=d*sc0; lo_f=d1*lo_nib - m1f, m1f=dmin*m0) — exactly the Q5 associativity §5 now requires. The new FP-associativity requirement is stated for BOTH formats: (d*sc_f)*q_f for Q6_K and (d*sc)*nib5 - (dmin*m) for Q5_K_M, in that exact grouping — matching both the kernel source (§4.1 line 171 'd*sc_f*q_f' is left-assoc; §3.2 line 126; §4.3 line 200 coopmat 'dsc*nib5 - dmm') and the template. Bit-exactness is by construction, not luck.
warnings: NON-BLOCKING (does NOT gate coding): the FIX-2 resolution re-points AT-2823 at the SAME q5k_dequant_matmul_f32accum_cpu oracle that AT-2822 already gates against at K=256 — so AT-2823 is now largely a duplicate of AT-2822's K=256 sub-case (same kernel, same oracle, same gate, same size). This is a redundant-coverage/efficiency observation, not a correctness hole: the spec itself notes cross-decode consistency is proven transitively by AT-2819 + AT-2822, which is exactly why AT-2823 no longer carries unique weight. If the Architect wants AT-2823 to earn its slot, it could instead use a DIFFERENT K or fixture than AT-2822's K=256 point, or fold into the AT-2824/2825 slack. Optional; APPROVE stands regardless.
spirv_concerns: No SPIR-V concern (unchanged from r1). Capability/extension set is unchanged from Q4_K_M; the AT-2813/2818/2821 cap-set-identity anchors mechanically enforce it. Portable Q6/Q5 kernels ride the same 8-bit-storage path AT-1520 already exercises on Lavapipe.
vendor_concerns: None new (unchanged from r1). Coopmat Q5 kernel inherits M3.6's NVIDIA sg==32 assumption and typed-skips on Lavapipe / sg!=32 (AT-2822). Portable kernels are vendor-neutral (f32 SSBOs).
missing_tests: Recommended (non-blocking, carried from r1): AT-2814/2819 fixture builders should ASSERT (not just intend) that every product w*x and every partial sum is exactly f32-representable (integer-valued, |partial| < 2^24) so the max_diff==0 claim is order-independent-safe. The spec states the property ('f16-exact integer-valued x so f32 accumulation is order-independent', AT-2814 line 296) and delegates to 'mirror AT-1520', which is acceptable; an in-builder assertion would make it robust to future fixture edits.
verified_ok: NO NEW HOLES from the r2 edits: §5 metric reuse (max_rel_diff/_combined/round_f32_to_f16_to_f32 from q4km_oracle) preserved as single source of truth; bit-exact fn q{6,5}k_dequant_matmul_f32_cpu takes native f32 x (matches template, exposed pub for dispatch tests); no regression to layouts, cap-set, phasing, dependency graph, or AT numbering.

TEMPLATE POINTER CONFIRMED IN-SOURCE: common_matmul.rs::q4km_dequant_matmul_cpu exists at line 118, uses stride 144/scales@+4/qs@+16, get_scale_min_k4, and the (d*sc)*nib - (dmin*m) grouping the spec now cites. The Coder can copy its per-element dequant + accumulation verbatim (adjusting stride/offsets/5th-bit for Q5, and the ql/qh 6-bit reassembly + signed path for Q6).

ACCUMULATION-ORDER handled correctly: for max_diff==0 the K-sum order need NOT match the kernel because AT-2814/2819 fixtures are integer-exact (associativity irrelevant); only the per-weight dequant GROUPING must match, and that is now explicitly stated for both formats. This is the AT-1520 discipline applied correctly.

LAYOUTS + SIGNEDNESS + ZERO-COMPILER-CHANGE (re-affirmed from r1, unchanged): Q6_K 210 B (ql@0/qh@128/scales int8@192/d@208, no dmin, 2-half/l/is=l/16, sc[8h+is+{0,2,4,6}]) and Q5_K_M 176 B (d@0/dmin@2/scales12@4/qh32@16/qs128@48, qh_bit_index=2*chunk+is_hi) match ggml byte-for-byte; the signed path is bit-exact-safe (f32_from_u32(u)-256.0 == (i8)u exactly for u in [128,255]); the 5 Q4_0 builtins + branch fully express both formats, and a genuinely-new builtin would fail-loud at compile.
M3.13 PERF CONCLUSION RESPECTED: no TFLOPS/leader gate; coverage-only. No closed perf question re-opened.
conditions: None. This is a clean APPROVE. The single non-blocking AT-2823-redundancy note and the AT-2814/2819 fixture-assertion recommendation are optional polish the Coder/QA may adopt; neither gates the start of coding.
